steps.decide: The reading measure, type scale and rhythm that make a long page readable
How the table of contents tracks position without stealing attention
How code, tables, callouts and images survive narrow widths
How deep links, anchors and print behave
How reading progress is exposed without a scroll-jacking bar

rules.statement: Body text holds a 65–75 character measure at every width; the column narrows with the viewport instead of holding a fixed pixel width.
The contents list shows the current section, uses aria-current='location', and never scroll-jacks; below 1024 px it collapses into a disclosure above the text.
Code blocks and tables scroll inside their own container with a visible affordance, never widening the page; images keep their aspect ratio and never exceed the measure.
Heading anchors are stable, copyable and focusable, with a visible target on approach; changing a heading's text must not silently break a published link.
Reading progress exists only as a 2 px indicator and never moves content; it is not announced and adds no motion under reduced-motion.
Printing removes chrome and expansion state, expands the contents list, and keeps URLs visible for citations.

sections.intent: Let a person read a long technical page at their own pace, jump to the part they need, and still find the section a week later from a link.
useCases: read a guide end to end on a phone
jump to the configuration section from a colleague's link
copy a code sample and confirm it belongs to this version
nicheDifferences: Read mode is judged by endurance rather than by first impression: a page that is beautiful for ten seconds and tiring for ten minutes has failed at the only job it had.
inputs: the longest realistic page length and the deepest heading level
whether code samples need copy affordances
whether the page is printed or cited
anatomy: one h1 and a visible hierarchy beneath it
a contents list with current-section state
prose measure, code and figure containers
heading anchors and a copy-link affordance
styling: one type family with a clear weight scale; code in a real monospace at a slightly smaller size
vertical rhythm from margins, not from dividers
anchors appear on hover and focus, never on scroll
a11y: heading levels are sequential and never skipped for size
code blocks are reachable and scrollable by keyboard with a visible scrollbar
the contents disclosure is a real button with expanded state
responsive: below 1024 px the contents list becomes a disclosure above the text, sticky to the top only while open
tables and code scroll inside their own container; the page never gains horizontal scroll
figures reflow to full measure with captions below
copy: section titles are verb phrases a reader would search for
code captions name the version the sample belongs to
anchor copy feedback says 'Link copied' and resets quietly
alternatives: a tutorial format with numbered steps when the reader must act in order
an interactive playground when the sample must be run
a changelog layout when the page is chronological by nature

references.label: HTML Living Standard — heading structure guidance

acceptance: body measure stays within 65–75 characters from 320 px to wide desktop
the contents list marks the current section and collapses below 1024 px
code and tables scroll internally without widening the page
every heading has a stable, copyable anchor that is focusable
printing removes chrome and expands the contents list
failureCases: a chapter of prose is set at 110 characters because the column is a percentage
the contents list hijacks scroll and the reader loses their place
a long code line widens the page and the mobile layout breaks
renaming a heading silently breaks published deep links
